scope: Static review of ordinary-RAM memfd v2 protocol/helper/client/broker, plus independent native helper tests; no core source changed by reviewer.
reviewed_properties: SETUP precedes backend lease creation; broker rejects protocol/sequence/session/body mismatch before creating the ordinary memfd.
Broker checks allowed client SO_PEERCRED; client checks configured service uid, socket directory ownership/type/mode, socket ownership/type and SO_PEERCRED.
Per-peer ordinary memfd has exact bounded capacity; setup carries fixed-width device/inode/seals, no DMA/device fd or physical/IOVA pointer.

Producer establishes shared RW map before F_SEAL_FUTURE_WRITE; required size/write/seal/exec seals are checked. Receiver requires exact setup seals, owner, type, zero links, nonexecutable mode, capacity/size, identity and FD_CLOEXEC.
Every setup fragment uses recvmsg, including server requests that require no descriptor. Extra or truncated rights and other ancillary types are rejected; received descriptors close on failure.
Receiver uses a shared readonly map with MADV_DONTFORK. Client closes received fd after mapping, checks pid before inherited mutex, refuses child API use and does not reconnect in the sandbox.
Client serializes request, metadata validation and copying from shared pixels into existing caller storage under its mutex; broker sends picture-only replies after copying into that connection slot.
Broker creates a separate memfd per connection; all normal serve exits free body and destroy producer mapping/fd before peer close. Setup failures route to the same cleanup.
Client validates positive OPEN session, strict response sequence/version/op/status, active session and requested dimensions, I420 size/capacity and picture color fields before copying.

tests.production_default: Native O2 PASS; silent 5005ms and drip-feed 5000ms with default 5000ms deadline

limits: Parent-owned end-to-end client/broker mock tests, aarch64 build, board deployment and Firefox RDD sandbox verification are separate acceptance gates.
No browser or video performance claim follows from helper tests or this static review.
MFD_NOEXEC_SEAL establishes immutable nonexecutable mode with F_SEAL_EXEC; review does not claim all executable mappings are prohibited.
Malformed ancillary tests cover cases representable by real Linux socket syscalls; arbitrary corrupted kernel-generated cmsghdr memory was not injected.
